# UX & Data-Trust Requirements Checklist: Dispatcher Console — Fleet State and Headway

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review ("unit tests for English") for the US-06 dispatcher console — fleet view, bunching/gap summary, data-trust shell, and accessibility.
**Created**: 2026-11-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete. Unchecked items are NOT an implementation blocker.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for each operational bus state (leader, regular, bunched, gap, broken down) including how each is presented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the fields shown per bus (state, position, headway-ahead, planned headway, data quality) fully enumerated in requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002/§FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements documented for the navigation shell's full element set (sidebar sections, corridor selector, clock, data-state badge, user identity, active-section marker)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the empty-state requirement (zero counts, informative message) specified for a corridor with no buses in service? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for the three source-status states (live, estimated, no data) and their corresponding indicator/banner behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006/§FR-007]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the spec define the explanatory banner content for the estimated state (which operator source is down) and no-data state (rely on the day's plan)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is the refresh cadence quantified rather than left vague? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009] — the spec states "approximately 5 seconds"; is the tolerance around that value defined for acceptance?
- [ ] CHK008 Is "leader-first" ordering defined unambiguously (by what the backend provides vs. any client-side ordering)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the "position along the corridor" representation specified clearly given there is no map (e.g., distance value, stop-relative label)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Assumption]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the no-data threshold ("no corridor events for more than 2 minutes") stated as a requirement rather than only an assumption? [Ambiguity, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "non-blocking stale-data indicator" defined with enough precision to distinguish it from the estimated/no-data banner? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the distinction between `data_quality` per-bus ("estimated") and overall `source_status` ("estimated") clear enough to avoid conflating them? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003/§FR-006]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Is the "estimated never raises an alert" rule stated consistently across the per-bus label requirement and the banner requirement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007/§FR-008]
- [ ] CHK014 Do the success criteria (SC-001..SC-007) each map to at least one functional requirement without contradiction? [Consistency, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the ~5 s cadence used consistently in the refresh requirement, the load-time criterion, and the freshness criterion? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009/§SC-001/§SC-002]
- [ ] CHK016 Are summary counts (buses in service, bunched, gaps) described consistently between the per-bus state requirements and the corridor summary requirement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004/§FR-005]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK017 Is each success criterion stated so it can be objectively verified against a served snapshot/fixture? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001..§SC-007]
- [ ] CHK018 Is "within 5 seconds of the view loading" (SC-001) measurable given the dependency on backend response time? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK019 Can "100% agreement" between displayed counts and the snapshot (SC-003) be objectively checked across the bunching/gap fixtures? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the recovery criterion (SC-006) measurable in terms of what "recovers automatically" and "without any crash or blank view" require? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the text-not-color criterion (SC-007) expressed so it can be verified for every state and data-quality condition? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007/§FR-012]

## Scenario & Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the single-bus / leader-only case where no bus-ahead headway exists? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for a broken-down bus (distinguishable, consistent in counts, no headway comparison)? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for state transitions between refreshes (e.g., live→estimated, ok→stale) updating without a reload? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases/§FR-014]
- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements defined for a backend briefly unreachable (retain last snapshot, retry next cadence, no crash)? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases/§FR-010]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for prolonged no-data persistence until fresh data resumes? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 Is behavior specified for a malformed body or schema-version mismatch (distinct from a normal refresh), or is it only in the data-model/contracts notes? [Gap, data-model.md Validation rules]
- [ ] CHK028 Are requirements defined for a null `headway_ahead_s` on a non-leader bus (not only the leader case)? [Coverage, data-model.md]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK029 Are accessibility requirements (text alongside color for all states; ARIA roles for status/alert/active-section) stated as requirements rather than only design-reference detail? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, Assumption: US-03 reference]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the polling/refresh behavior's non-functional expectation (no manual reload, background-tab behavior) specified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK031 Are the Turn-1 performance boundaries (no sub-2 s refresh, no streaming) stated as scope rather than implied? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK032 Are resilience requirements (graceful degradation to stale) defined independently of the data-quality/source-status requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK033 Is the dependency on the backend read API (corridor snapshot + source-status feeds) documented and its availability treated as a precondition? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the assumption that the US-03 desktop styling spec is the authoritative visual/interaction reference validated and its scope (shell vs. fleet content) delimited? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions / plan.md]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the single-corridor scope (C6-008, direction 1) and the exclusion of multi-corridor/second-direction/short-turning stated explicitly? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK036 Is the read-only/no-auth scope (user identity presentational, no access-control decisions in the frontend) documented as an assumption and a constraint? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the contract-version dependency (schemas pinned at v1.0.0, types generated and never hand-edited) captured as a requirement/assumption the console depends on? [Dependency, contracts/README.md]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK038 Is there any ambiguity between "visually distinguish" (FR-004) and the text-not-color rule (FR-012) that needs reconciling into one measurable expectation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004/§FR-012]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the no-data threshold value reconciled between the spec assumption and the source-status "sources_down > 2 min" semantics so there is one authoritative definition? [Conflict, Spec Assumptions / data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK040 Is the term "stale" (connection) kept clearly distinct from "estimated"/"no_data" (source status) everywhere the two could be confused by a reviewer? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010/§FR-006]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state but must not modify markers; unchecked items here are a reviewer aid, not an implementation gate.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`.
